blocks.text: In both English and Russian adjectives and adverbs have three forms, which are called degrees: positive, comparative, superlative — good, better, best; fast, faster, fastest.

The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "-ее" (sometimes shortened to "-ей") to the stem of the adjective: новый — новее; красивый — красивее. This comparative form is the same for all genders and the plural. It is not declined and can be used as a predicate only.

Note the stress. If the word consists of two syllables, the stress is on the comparative ending "-ее": новый — новее; старый — старее. Other adjectives as a rule have the same stress in both the basic and the comparative forms: свободный — свободнее; интересный — интереснее. There are some exceptions: здоровый — здоровее, тяжёлый — тяжелее, холодный — холоднее, весёлый — веселее, горячий — горячее.

Many adverbs which end in "о" are formed from adjectives … The comparative degree of these adverbs is formed in the same way as the comparative of adjectives: *Он идёт быстро. Я иду быстрее. Там было холодно. Здесь ещё холоднее.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 80, 82.
